## Analysis set and estimand

This report estimates the **available-case modified ITT contrast in this model's fitted analysis set**. Of 57 children randomised, the published CONSORT diagram records three losses to follow-up—one intervention child and two waiting-control children—leaving 54 analysed and represented in the repository. It separately records that two children in each arm discontinued the intervention but were followed and included in the analyses; this model likewise retains children under their assigned arm rather than conditioning on adherence. The model additionally requires its outcome, baseline and any named robustness covariates to be observed. It is therefore an available-case modified ITT analysis, not an unqualified full-population ITT. Randomisation balances the original assigned arms in expectation; it does not guarantee balance after loss to follow-up or further observed-data restrictions. A causal reading even for the fitted contrast therefore assumes that loss to follow-up, outcome observation and any further complete-case restriction did not select children differently between arms according to their potential outcomes, after allowing for the stated pre-treatment information. Interpreting the contrast as the effect for all 57 randomised children requires further assumptions about the missing outcomes and a corresponding attrition sensitivity. Any extra complete-case restriction is stated in the model overview.

The bridge and MAR rows average both potential-outcome surfaces over common sets of 53 and 57 profiles, respectively. MAR assumes that outcome observation is independent of the unseen t2 score conditional on assigned arm, screening word reading and screening age, together with the fitted logit Beta-Binomial outcome model and covariate overlap; posterior-predictive checks cannot test that identifying assumption. Jump-to-reference and the 25 delta rows answer a different factual-completion question: they compare the 29 assigned-intervention profiles with the 28 assigned-control profiles, modifying only the unavailable outcome in its assigned arm. The zero-delta row is that factual-arm MAR anchor. The no-benefit restriction gives the one intervention non-starter the control mean surface; it is not classical distributional reference-based multiple imputation. The other rows shift the one intervention and three waiting-control missing outcomes on the 79-item scale. Counterfactual response status is not identified. The fixed shifts are diagnostic identifying restrictions, not estimated parameters or a probability distribution over departures from MAR. Predictions that reach a physical test bound are clipped, and the clipped fractions are reported.\n\n:::"
```{python}
    )
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
from language_reading_predictors.statistical_models.reporting import odds_string as _odds

if tau_summary is not None:
    _t = tau_summary.iloc[0]
    # New artefacts name the headline direction by estimand and scale. Fall back
    # only so previously fitted reports can still render.
    _prob_ame_pos = float(
        _t["prob_ame_pos"]
        if "prob_ame_pos" in tau_summary.columns
        else _t["prob_tau_pos"]
    )
    _items = f" (≈ **{_t.tau_prob_median * n_trials:+.1f} items**)" if n_trials else ""
    _lab = (
        f", *{_t.direction_label} evidence*"
        if "direction_label" in tau_summary.columns
        else ""
    )
    print(
        f"On the probability scale the average marginal randomised-arm contrast on "
        f"{outcome_label} is **{_t.tau_prob_median:+.3f}** (risk difference){_items} "
        f"(central 50% credible interval {_t.tau_prob_lo50:+.3f} to {_t.tau_prob_hi50:+.3f}; "
        f"89% {_t.tau_prob_lo:+.3f} to {_t.tau_prob_hi:+.3f}). "
        f"P(intervention helps) = {_prob_ame_pos:.3f} ({_odds(_prob_ame_pos)}{_lab})."
    )
    if str(_t.get("favoured_direction", "positive")) == "negative":
        print(
            f"\n\n_The favoured direction is **harm**: evidence the intervention is "
            f"harmful is *{_t.favoured_direction_label}* (P = "
            f"{_t.favoured_direction_prob:.3f}). The label above is for the "
            f"'intervention helps' claim only._"
        )
    if "tau_prob_hpdi_lo" in tau_summary.columns:
        print(
            f"\n\n_Sensitivity — the 89% highest posterior density interval (HPDI) on the "
            f"probability scale is {_t.tau_prob_hpdi_lo:+.3f} to {_t.tau_prob_hpdi_hi:+.3f}. "
            f"The HPDI is not transformation-invariant, so it is a scale-specific check, "
            f"not a replacement for the equal-tailed interval._"
        )
    if not n_trials_confirmed:
        print(
            "\n\n_Items-scale figures for this outcome are approximate — the test "
            "ceiling (`n_trials`) is unconfirmed._"
        )
    # Monte-Carlo precision of the DERIVED probability-scale AME. The convergence
    # gate scans the model parameters; this reports the sampling precision of the
    # post-processed estimand itself (guarded — appears once the fit carries the
    # columns). Bulk-ESS governs the median; Tail-ESS the 89% interval limits.
    if "tau_prob_ess_tail" in tau_summary.columns and np.isfinite(
        _t.get("tau_prob_ess_tail", float("nan"))
    ):
        _mcse_items = (
            f" (≈ {_t.tau_prob_mcse_median * n_trials:.2g} items)" if n_trials else ""
        )
        print(
            f"\n\n_Monte-Carlo precision of this derived average marginal effect: "
            f"Bulk-ESS {_t.tau_prob_ess_bulk:,.0f}, Tail-ESS {_t.tau_prob_ess_tail:,.0f} "
            f"(the 89% equal-tailed limits are governed by Tail-ESS), median MCSE "
            f"{_t.tau_prob_mcse_median:.4f}{_mcse_items} — the sampling precision of the "
            f"post-processed estimand itself, distinct from the parameter-level gate._"
        )
```

- `tau_logit_*`: posterior median and equal-tailed central interval (coverage `ci_prob`) of $\tau$ on the logit scale.
- `tau_prob_*`: average marginal randomised-arm contrast on the probability scale (risk difference), averaged over the fitted available-case analysis set per posterior draw.
- `tau_*_lo/hi`, `tau_*_lo50/hi50`: the fixed posterior-band convention (#177, revised 2026-07-17) — the equal-tailed **89%** headline interval (`_lo/_hi`) and the **central 50%** interval (`_lo50/_hi50`, the middle half of the posterior mass; a visual aid, not a threshold), reported alongside the full posterior. Direction is read from `prob_ame_pos`, never from whether a band excludes zero.
- `tau_*_hpdi_lo/hi`: 89% highest posterior density interval (HPDI) at the same coverage — a per-scale sensitivity companion to the equal-tailed interval. The HPDI is not transformation-invariant, so it is reported separately on the logit and probability scales, not mapped between them.
- `prob_ame_pos`: posterior probability that the probability-scale average marginal effect is positive, $P(\operatorname{AME} > 0) = P(\text{intervention helps})$; this is the headline direction probability and `direction_label` is its round-odds evidence label.
- `prob_tau_logit_pos`: posterior probability that the conditional logit-scale treatment coefficient is positive. It is secondary and can differ from `prob_ame_pos` when treatment is moderated across children.
- `prob_tau_pos`: backward-compatible alias of `prob_ame_pos`. New code should use `prob_ame_pos`; the report falls back to this alias only for pre-schema artefacts.

```{python}
        "distribution is real predictive uncertainty for one child: parameter uncertainty plus "

        "average effect is well supported."
```

### Intervention vs no-intervention overlap

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
if _has("arm_overlap_mean.png"):
    print(_img("arm_overlap_mean.png", "Posterior of each arm's population-average expected outcome, overlaid"))
    print(
        f"\n_How to read it:_ two smoothed posterior curves for the model's population-average "
        f"expected {outcome_label} — no intervention (grey) and intervention (blue) — with the "
        "overlapping area shaded and each arm's median marked. The **overlap fraction** is an "
        "at-a-glance summary of how distinguishable the arms are: near-separate curves mean a "
        "confidently signed effect, heavily overlapping curves mean the arms are hard to tell "
        "apart. The annotated average contrast and P(intervention higher) are the same guard-tested "
        "quantities as the ROPE summary above; the plotted numbers are in `arm_overlap_mean.csv`."
    )
    print(
        '\n::: {.callout-note title="Overlap of the arms vs uncertainty about the difference"}\n\n'
        "These two curves share the untreated linear predictor within each posterior draw, so "
        "they are positively correlated — their *marginal* overlap can look larger than the "
        "uncertainty in the **difference** actually is. Read the effect itself from the ROPE / "
        "effect density above; this figure is the intuitive companion, not a replacement.\n\n:::\n"
    )
```
